flagship.headline: The Beatles begin recording Strawberry Fields Forever
flagship.summary_line_1: The Beatles began recording Strawberry Fields Forever in Studio Two at EMI Studios, Abbey Road, on November 24, 1966, per the Beatles Bible.
flagship.summary_line_2: It was their first session after quitting touring, Paul McCartney played a Mellotron for the flute-like opening, and the clip below is the finished song.

events.headline: The Beatles release Hello, Goodbye in the UK
events.summary_line_1: Parlophone released the Beatles' single Hello, Goodbye (R 5655), backed with I Am the Walrus, in the UK on November 24, 1967, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It spent seven weeks at No. 1 in the UK and three on the US Hot 100, and the clip below is the A-side.

events.headline: The Beatles begin recording Strawberry Fields Forever
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles began recording Strawberry Fields Forever in Studio Two at EMI Studios, Abbey Road, on November 24, 1966, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It was their first session after quitting touring, Paul McCartney played a Mellotron for the flute-like opening, and the clip below is the finished song.

events.headline: The Who start a Tuesday residency at the Marquee
events.summary_line_1: The Who began a Tuesday night residency at the Marquee Club in London on November 24, 1964, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It ran for sixteen weeks, broke the club's attendance records and built their reputation, and the clip below is I Can't Explain, their first single as the Who, released in January 1965.

events.headline: Paul McCartney's father Jim marries Angela Williams
events.summary_line_1: Jim McCartney, father of Paul McCartney, married Angela Williams on November 24, 1964, per the Paul McCartney Project, eight years after the death of his first wife, Mary.
events.summary_line_2: Angela said they took a taxi to Carrog in North Wales for the ceremony, per her ClassicBands interview, and the clip below is the Beatles' I Feel Fine, released three days later.

events.headline: The Beatles play the ABC Cinema in Hull
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the ABC Cinema in Hull, Yorkshire, on Sunday, November 24, 1963, their third performance in the city, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: They were mid-tour and five days from releasing I Want to Hold Your Hand in the UK, and the clip below is that song.

events.headline: The Four Seasons hold No. 1 with Big Girls Don't Cry
events.summary_line_1: Big Girls Don't Cry by the Four Seasons was No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated November 24, 1962, the second of its five weeks on top, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It followed the Crystals' He's a Rebel at the top and held until Telstar took over, and the clip below is the Four Seasons single.
